Definition: from G575 and G1166; to show off, i.e. exhibit; figuratively, to demonstrate, i.e. accredit:--(ap-)prove, set forth, shew.
BiblicalUsage: To show off, to exhibit, to prove by putting on display. Peter tells the men of Israel that Jesus was a man approved of God among them by miracles and wonders and signs in Acts 2:22 — God put the proof where everyone could see it. Paul says the apostles have been set forth last, as it were appointed to death, made a spectacle unto the world in 1 Corinthians 4:9, and the man of sin will sit in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God in 2 Thessalonians 2:4.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that God proves His servants the same way the enemy proves his — in public, before witnesses. The difference is the proof itself: miracles and wonders for Jesus, suffering and death for the apostles, and a lying display for the man of sin. I am to read the display, not the claim.
